title: PAR-03 unassigned DXF ranges and binary raw-width refusal
mode: Source-backed local classifier and writer fast slice

localScope.head: de27a33
localScope.worktreeState: The shared worktree was already broadly dirty. This slice updates the DXF classifier and binary string sink, extends generated tests, and records progress; nothing was staged or committed.

evidence.finding: The cited Autodesk value-type and numerical references do not assign general types to 150-159 or 180-209. This does not exclude private or contextual producer uses; no binary width is inferred from adjacent ranges.

implementation.change: The standalone classifier marks 150-159 and 180-209 Unknown; the explicit LibreCadMasterLegacy profile retains the previous string interpretation. Binary DXF writeRawString no longer emits unknown codes as guessed NUL-terminated strings. Existing standalone 80-89 unknown handling and code-1009 string handling remain covered.
assertions: ASCII readers retain opaque spellings for representative codes in both unknown spans.
Standalone binary readers and both typed/raw binary string writers refuse unknown widths.
The explicit legacy profile writes and reads historical string values at codes 150, 180, and 209.
Known string values remain available through the binary raw-string API.
implementation.claimBoundary: This resolves only these classifier/writer width decisions. It does not complete the full PAR-03 code-by-code/context audit or establish broad DXF interoperability or format support. Codes 240-259 and the standalone 260-269 interpretation remain open for separate evidence-led review.

commands.command: git diff --check -- src/intern/dxfcode.h src/intern/dxfwriter.cpp src/intern/dxfwriter.h tests/wave1_tests.cpp tests/hardening_tests.cpp

nextAction: Continue the evidence-led PAR-03 audit for the 240-259 contextual callers and the standalone 260-269 assignment; preserve explicit legacy behavior and do not infer binary widths.
